subject: Private deployment: version sheltering & maintenance coordination
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@acme.com>, acme-prodops@acme.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: version sheltering & maintenance coordination

Hi Jill / Acme ops,

Following our runbook review, we want to propose a detailed maintenance approach for the private VPC deployment that minimizes risk while allowing the security patches and a small runtime upgrade. High level plan below — please flag any hard constraints ASAP so we can refine.

Summary of proposal:
- Target: apply security patches + minor runtime bump (current: redwood-private 2.11.1 -> 2.12.0-rc2).
- Version sheltering: pin customer fleet to 2.11.1 while we stage canaries on a parallel slice. This prevents accidental drift for long-tailed tenants during rollout.
- Maintenance window candidates: Saturday 02:00–06:00 EST (we expect up to a 4-hour window, but typical impact should be limited to rolling restarts and warmup).
- Canary -> ramp: 10% canary (30m), evaluate telemetry (latency, error-rate, KV cache miss), then 30% (30m), then full ramp.
- Rollback: immediate automatic rollback to pinned 2.11.1 if error-rate > 2x baseline or P90 latency crosses +200ms for 3 consecutive minutes. Manual rollback checklist included.
- Operational steps: graceful connection drain, KV cache pre-warm (preview step), health-check gating, and circuit-breaker thresholds.

Attachments: maintenance_runbook.pdf (draft), diff-checklist.csv.

Open questions for Acme:
1) Any blackout windows in that Saturday window?
2) Can we run a short dry-run on non-prod staging (we recommend Wed 23:00–00:30 EST) to validate the pin/unpin automation?
3) Are there any compliance gating steps (audit snapshot, logs export) you want completed before the start?

We'll have Karthik lead the rollout engineering and Neha own the post-upgrade validation metrics. If that looks good I'll convert the draft runbook into a final Doc and schedule the shiproom.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.com
Attachments: maintenance_runbook.pdf (application/pdf, 480KB); diff-checklist.csv (text/csv, 8KB)

Thanks Priyom — good summary. A few constraints from our side:

- Blackout: our trading ingestion batch runs Friday 23:30–00:30 EST and Monday 05:00–06:30 EST. Saturday 02:00–06:00 EST is preferred but we cannot exceed 2 hours of any customer-visible downtime.
- Compliance: we require an audit snapshot of logs and a retention-of-evidence bundle exported to our secure S3 (link will be shared by our security team) before any version flip.
- KV cache concern: the main risk we saw previously was a slow warm-up causing elevated latency for 10–15 minutes post-start. Can you confirm pre-warm steps and whether we can do a warm standby node pre-filled with KV entries?

Also cc'ing acme-prodops who will triage infra constraints.

Jill
Jill Park
Head of Platform Operations, Acme Financial Services

Thanks — quick technical reply and concrete mitigations.

Quoted for clarity:
On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jill Park <jill.park@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Priyom — good summary. A few constraints from our side:
> 
> - Blackout: ... Saturday 02:00–06:00 EST is preferred but we cannot exceed 2 hours of any customer-visible downtime.

Acknowledged. Planning notes and changes to the draft plan:

1) Window & impact budget
- We'll keep the Saturday 02:00–06:00 EST slot as the nominal window but will cap any customer-visible interruption to 2 hours. To stay within that budget we'll favor parallel canaries (slices) over full sequential restarts and increase overlap for KV pre-warm (see preflight step).

2) Version sheltering mechanics
- Implementation: maintain a "shelter" flag in the control plane that pins traffic routing for tenant X to the existing 2.11.1 image while we bake 2.12.0-rc2 in an isolated slice. The flag can be toggled via the ops API with a single-call rollback.
- Canary sizing: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> full. Each stage 20–40 minutes depending on metrics. We will abort earlier if thresholds trigger.

3) KV pre-warm strategy
- Maintain a warm-standby pod pool with preloaded KV cache for critical tenant keys (we'll use your representative keyset). During canary we route a small amount of replay traffic to validate TTLs and hit-rate. This reduces the first-10-minute tail risk.

4) Telemetry & gating
- Gate on: P50/P90 latency, error-rate, model-inference failures, and redis-miss percent. Primary abort triggers: error-rate > 2x baseline OR P90 > baseline +200ms for >3m.

5) Rollback specifics
- Auto-rollback: control-plane check runs every 30s during ramp; if triggered it initiates an automated rollback to 2.11.1 and drains new pods.
- Manual fallback: runbook includes command set to force-pin, and an emergency unpin script. The attached shelter-preflight-notes.txt has the commands.

6) Dry-run
- We can run the dry-run on staging Wed (23:00–00:30 EST). We'll capture diagnostic snapshots and share the evidence bundle to your S3 bucket prior to Saturday.

7) Audit snapshot & evidence export
- We will export audit logs and a signed snapshot to the provided S3 path before the version flip and include the DocuSign audit confirmation (DocuSign:DS-83472).

Attachments added to this reply: shelter-preflight-notes.txt (commands & gating thresholds). I also updated the runbook in the shared Drive link.

If this aligns with Acme constraints we will finalize the runbook and schedule the shiproom.

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
